opus.market_notes: One-tap orbit hoppers are a heavily saturated hyper-casual niche (Orbit, Planet Hop, many clones), and nothing here really sets it apart. Success depends on paid UA and ad monetization, and it has neither yet.
opus.summary: This is a solid one-tap orbit prototype. It has a real hazard progression (collapsing planets, black holes, asteroids, flippers, laser gates, Hard and Daily modes) plus missions, achievements and skins, and the bot-driven tests all pass. The art is AI-generated and decent-looking, but the busy nebula backgrounds hide gameplay and swamp the small comet. The HUD is stacked text and the menu uses emoji buttons. Audio is synthesized WebAudio only, with no composed music. Ads stop at a bridge stub, no native projects exist, and the store screenshots have weak gameplay framing, so it can't ship today.
blockers: No ad or IAP SDK: ads.js is a no-op bridge, so there's no AdMob/UMP/ATT, no remove-ads purchase, and Continue/2x stay hidden, which leaves zero revenue
No native iOS/Android projects or device testing; haptics plugin not bundled; ~15MB of full-res nebula/splash PNGs bloat the bundle and may cost frame rate and memory on low-end phones

Gameplay readability: busy photoreal nebula backgrounds bury the comet, orbit ring and hazards; a planet overlaps the HUD; the HUD is a pile of text lines (ALIGN 94°, laser countdowns) instead of visual cues
Store assets not ready: gameplay screenshot shows score 0 and no visible action, 1080x1920 Android set and preview video missing, assets/icon-1024.png still a placeholder, privacy policy not hosted
Thin onboarding and presentation: one-line text tutorial, emoji menu buttons (🏆🔊⚙), no composed music, and no real human playtest tuning of the difficulty curve
